descriptionChirho: To obliterate a written record, name, or sin by blotting out — used of God or humans erasing sins, names from a book, or memory of something (Qal active).
To physically wipe a surface clean or wipe away tears — a concrete, tactile action of cleaning or drying by rubbing (Qal active).
To annihilate or exterminate living beings from the earth — used especially of the Flood narrative and divine judgment destroying all life (Qal active).
To be erased, obliterated, or destroyed — the Nifal passive expressing that a name, memory, or people are blotted out or wiped away.
To cause destruction or bring to ruin — the Hifil causative stem expressing the bringing about of obliteration or annihilation.
